mechanism_narrative: An increase in the Consumer Price Index (CPIAUCSL) above 2% YoY signals inflationary pressures that typically lead to tighter monetary policy, which in turn increases borrowing costs and reduces corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or CPIAUCSL YoY > 2% does not correlate with subsequent tightening cycles.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) by more than 0.5% in a month signals a weakening labor market, which typically precedes an economic slowdown, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or UNRATE increase > 0.5% does not correlate with subsequent economic slowdowns.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in real GDP (GDPC1) over two consecutive quarters signals a recessionary environment, which leads to reduced consumer spending and corporate earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 60-day returns in > 50% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or GDPC1 decline does not correlate with subsequent recessionary environments.

mechanism_narrative: A significant increase in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a robust supply-side expansion, which typically leads to increased corporate profits and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or INDPRO increase > 1% does not correlate with subsequent corporate profit growth.

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) is above 6%, it signals an accommodative monetary policy in a weak labor market, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days as investors anticipate economic recovery.
regime_hint: accommodative monetary policy in a weak labor market
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 20-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of low FEDFUNDS and high UNRATE does not correlate with subsequent economic recovery.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in housing starts (HOUST) signals a strengthening demand for housing, which typically leads to increased economic activity and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 60-day returns in > 40% of instances despite the positive signal, or HOUST increase does not correlate with subsequent economic activity growth.

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payroll employment (PAYEMS) increases by more than 200,000 jobs in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases, it signals a strengthening labor market, which typically leads to increased consumer spending and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces negative 5-day returns in > 40% of triggered instances despite the positive signal, or the combination of PAYEMS increase and UNRATE decrease does not correlate with subsequent consumer spending growth.

mechanism_narrative: A significant decline in retail sales (RSAFS) signals weakening consumer demand, which typically leads to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 produces positive 20-day returns in > 60% of triggered instances despite the negative signal, or RSAFS decline does not correlate with subsequent corporate earnings reduction.
